guitar.type: Solid-body electric guitars with single-coil pickups
guitar.modelsText: Fender Bullet Stratocasters documented during the Wolfgang Amadeus Phoenix sessions; the exact guitar and guitarist for each 1901 part are not identified
guitar.evidence: The album credits list Christian Mazzalai and Laurent Brancowitz on guitar. A contemporary EQ Magazine studio feature states that both guitarists used Fender Bullet Stratocasters for the album and describes the guitar tracks as clipped, dry and artificial. Brancowitz independently confirmed his use of a Fender Bullet and minimal effects. No reliable source assigns a specific 1901 guitar take, pickup position or tuning to either guitarist.
guitar.notes: Most album guitars were recorded dry, often through a direct box, high-grade preamp and hardware compression. Standard tuning is a practical assumption, not a documented session fact. The large fuzzy chords specifically documented on 1901 came from a Korg Trident synthesizer, not from a fuzz guitar.
guitar.source: Patrick Sisson, EQ Magazine, "Champagne and Plastic: Phoenix Mixes Experimentation, Perfectionism, and Distractions to Produce Wolfgang Amadeus Phoenix" — https://patricksisson.com/champagne-and-plastic-phoenix-mixes-experimentation-perfectionism-and-distractions-to-produce-wolfgang-amadeus-phoenix/ ; MusicRadar, "Phoenix's Laurent 'Branco' Brancowitz on their astonishing 2009" — https://www.musicradar.com/news/guitars/phoenixs-laurent-branco-brancowitz-on-their-astonishing-2009-230064 ; Wolfgang Amadeus Phoenix release credits — https://www.discogs.com/release/14160445-Phoenix-Wolfgang-Amadeus-Phoenix

tone.target: 1901 — 2009 Wolfgang Amadeus Phoenix studio version, rhythm-guitar layer
tone.profile: dry, clipped and compressed single-coil rhythm tone with low gain and firm upper-mid attack
tone.summary: The guitar contribution is tighter and drier than the current chorus-heavy preset. It behaves like a compressed direct or very clean amplified signal, while much of the apparent width and fuzz comes from layered synthesizers and production.
gearClues: fuzzy sustained layers supplied mainly by Korg Trident synthesizer
corrections: replace the Fender or JC claim with a dry studio-chain adaptation
identify the prominent fuzzy chords as synthesizer rather than guitar

rig.name: Phoenix - 1901 Studio Rhythm - Valeton GP-180
rig.recommendedGuitar: Fender Bullet S-1 or Strat-style guitar with low-output single-coil pickups; start with the bridge pickup

blocks.referenceModel: Telefunken U73 or UREI 1176 studio compression
blocks.purpose: Approximate the controlled studio dynamics and clipped consistency of the recorded guitar layers.
blocks.gap: The GP-180 compressor cannot reproduce the documented studio preamp, direct-box and hardware-compressor chain exactly.

blocks.purpose: Provide a low-gain, fast and neutral platform that approximates the dry direct-recording character through FRFR equipment.
blocks.gap: No amplifier has been reliably documented for the individual 1901 guitar takes. Album guitars were commonly recorded through a direct box and studio electronics.

alternatives.reason: Use for a firmer and cleaner live-style response; Fender Twin amplifiers are documented for Phoenix live rigs but not for the 1901 studio take.
Use only for a more chiming studio variation; Phoenix reported having a Vox amplifier in the studio, but its use on 1901 is unconfirmed.

blocks.purpose: Keep the FRFR output compact and articulate without adding a large or dark cabinet character.
blocks.gap: A cabinet is required for a practical FRFR preset, although the documented album workflow often used direct guitar recording.

alternatives.reason: Pair with Foxy 30TB when testing the unconfirmed Vox-style studio variation.
Use with a neutral open-back 1x12 or 2x12 IR if the stock cabinet sounds too rounded.

blocks.referenceModel: Helios preamp and console filtering used during album mixing
blocks.purpose: Reduce low-end masking and retain the narrow, plastic upper-mid character described by the guitarists and producer.
blocks.gap: The broad GP-180 EQ cannot reproduce the documented combination of studio preamps, console filters and analogue equalizers.

alternatives.reason: Use when narrower control is needed to reduce harshness or emphasize the pick attack.

improvements.summary: The main remaining limitation is the absence of a dedicated direct-to-console guitar path and studio-grade compression model.

proposals.reason: A restrained IR can reduce the stronger cabinet coloration of the stock US 2x12 model.
proposals.whenToUse: Use after matching gain and compression at rehearsal volume.
proposals.expectedGain: Tighter transients and a less obviously modelled cabinet sound.

proposals.recommendedAsset: Second independently played guitar take or doubled recording
proposals.reason: The studio width should come from arrangement and production rather than an audible chorus block.
proposals.whenToUse: Use for recording or when two guitarists reproduce the song.
proposals.expectedGain: More authentic width without modulation blur.
